promptHead: Athlete goal: 5K (Corrowmore Harvest 5K) on Sun Nov 15 2026, 10 weeks out, target run the whole way.

new.headline: Great start, and the honest answer is no, do not run every day; we build the race by nudging what you already do, not by piling on days.

flags.title: Adding days too soon
flags.detail: beginner legs break down when run days jump from 3 to 7, so we stay at 3 and add a little time instead.

flags.title: Tight calves next morning
flags.detail: still clearing by the following day, which is fine; tell me if it lingers past 48 hours.

answers.question: I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?
answers.answer:
No, please do not run every day next week. You are 10 weeks out and the race is well within reach on three run days a week, which is what you have been doing.

The gains from a run happen on the rest day that follows it. Running daily this early almost always leads to sore shins, grumpy calves or an Achilles that forces time off, and that would cost you more than it buys. Your dog walks on the other days are perfect active recovery.

The plan is to grow the three runs you already do by a minute or two each week, and lengthen Saturday a bit more. Ten weeks of that gets you to the finish line running.

new.analysis:
You did the hardest part, which is starting, and the numbers back up how well you paced it. Heart rate sat in zone 2 for most of each run, drift was tiny, and pain was 0/10 on all three. That is exactly how a first week should look.

The build this week is small on purpose. Monday and Wednesday go up by about two minutes each, Saturday gets a touch longer, and the walk-run ratio stays the same so nothing new is asked of your legs at once. Total time on feet moves from about 64 to about 72 minutes, which is a sensible step for someone three weeks into running.

Calves tightening the day after is normal at this stage and the fact that it clears overnight is a good sign. Keep walking the dog on the off days, because easy movement helps those calves more than sitting still does. If any soreness sharpens, lingers past two days, or shows up as a specific spot rather than general tightness, back off and tell me.

One habit worth starting now: a couple of minutes of easy walking before you begin the run intervals, and another couple at the end. It makes the first run interval feel better and the calves happier the next morning.

safetyCallouts.title: Tell me if calf tightness changes character.
safetyCallouts.body: If it sharpens, lingers past two days, or settles into one spot, ease off and consider seeing a physio rather than running through it.
